source.title: DriveVLA-W0: World Models Amplify Data Scaling Law in Autonomous Driving
source.authors: Ying-Yan Li; Shu-Yao Shang; Wei-Song Liu; Bing Zhan; Hao-Chen Wang; Yu-Quan Wang; Yun-Tao Chen; Xiao-Man Wang; Ya-Song An; Chu-Feng Tang; Lu Hou; Lue Fan; Zhao-Xiang Zhang

record.file_problem: None; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: Applies data-scaling and world-model results to autonomous-driving models, a new domain and training setting relative to language-model pretraining scaling laws.
record.gate_note: The paper does not measure held-out language-model cross-entropy, parameter/token/compute scaling, or fit power laws. Its relevant results are driving-task metrics over dataset sizes and a decoder comparison across two data regimes. Other benchmark comparisons and ablations not varying data scale do not bear directly on these versions.
record.test_reason: Trains driving VLA and TransFuser models at 70k, 700k and 70M frames, about three orders of magnitude, and reports task error at each size. This bears on V5, data scaling in a fine-tuning regime outside text pretraining. No power law is fitted. Most of the paper is a comparison of its own method against baselines.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that world modeling (future-image prediction) amplifies data scaling of driving VLAs: action-only baselines plateau while the VLA-W0 models keep improving, most clearly at 70M frames. They also report that the autoregressive decoder overtakes flow-matching and query-based decoders at large data scale. The cited 28.8% ADE gain is for the VQ model, whose true rows the record mislabeled.
record.recipe_differences: Studies data scaling in autonomous-driving VLA models using ADE, collision rate, and benchmark planning scores, rather than language-model held-out cross-entropy scaling against parameters, tokens, and compute. No power-law fitting or compute-optimal allocation is performed.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported advantage varies by model architecture, metric, and data scale: VQ and ViT results differ, and the VQ world-model condition is worse than its baseline on both reported metrics at 700k frames and on collision rate at 70M frames. Action-decoder rankings also differ between NAVSIM and the 70M-frame in-house setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding a world-model (future-image) objective changes the data-scaling slope. The true VQ ADE at 70M is 1.0563 with the world model versus 1.4829 action-only.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Auxiliary dense self-supervision steepens data scaling of fine-tuned VLA driving models.

fits_no_version.finding: The action-decoder ranking reverses between NAVSIM (about 100k frames) and in-house 70M frames: query-based is best small, autoregressive is best large.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The relative ranking of output-head designs can invert with data scale.

fits_no_version.finding: TransFuser-7B is not better than TransFuser-50M (NAVSIM PDMS 77.9 vs 79.2 from scratch; in-house ADE 2.14 vs 1.75 at 700k).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Parameter scaling gives no gain for sparse-action-supervised driving models at these data sizes.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for the scaling results. Only three data sizes are evaluated; no power-law fit, exponent, or prediction from smaller runs is provided. The in-house test set comprises 100 challenging scenarios. Results vary by architecture and metric.
record.rows_left_out: No other data-scale results from the main text or appendix were left out. Non-scaling benchmark results and unrelated ablations are omitted.

untested.parts: No language-model held-out loss and no parameter, token or compute power law.
No shape ablation at fixed parameter count.
Power-law functional form: no fit, only three data sizes, no uncertainty. No parameter or compute scaling curve, no repeated-data study, no image or video generative scaling.
No downstream prediction from scale or pretraining loss. The driving metrics are the fine-tuned task's own error.
No comparison of fitting choices or exponents.

missing.what: TransFuser-50M vs 7B on NAVSIM, from scratch and pretrained (PDMS 79.2/77.9; 83.6/71.6)
missing.versions: V5 (parameter scaling; none if strictly data)

missing.what: Collision rate at 700k, 7M and 70M frames for VLA, VLA-W0 and TransFuser, including a 7M point

record.verdict_notes: Table 3 text extraction places model labels after their numbers. The first unlabeled block is TransFuser-50M/7B, which the reader mislabeled as VLA (VQ); this is confirmed by the text's 28.8% and 15.9% figures. Only three data sizes are used, with no uncertainty and a 100-scenario test set. 'Scaling law' is used loosely: no power law is fitted.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out language-model pretraining loss or power-law relationship with parameters, tokens, or compute is measured.
No power laws are fitted on small runs and used to predict larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation between parameters and tokens is studied.
No comparison isolates depth, width, or architecture at a fixed parameter count.

Tests data-scale behavior in autonomous driving, not whether the same power-law functional form holds: it reports no fitted exponents or power-law fit. It does not study image/video generative-model scaling generally, repeated data, or fine-tuning/transfer power laws.
Reports driving-task outcomes at selected training-data sizes, but does not fit a predictive relationship or test downstream-task prediction from pretraining loss.
Does not compare fitting choices or estimate setup-dependent scaling exponents or compute-optimal allocations.

relationships.condition: All models, in-house data 70k→700k→70M frames, ADE
relationships.reason: Error falls at every size, but the per-decade gain shrinks sharply after 700k (e.g. ViT baseline 0.45× then about 0.88×/decade), bending away from a single power law.
relationships.display_finding: Error fell at every data scale, but the ViT baseline's error multiplier weakened from 0.45 to about 0.88 per decade after 700k frames.

relationships.reason: From the text (rows missing): ADE 1.5424→1.4829 over two decades, which the authors call saturation. The trend depends on the training objective.
relationships.display_finding: ADE decreased only from 1.5424 to 1.4829 across two decades of data, which the authors described as saturation.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
